vector.description: Host conformance (§16.3): the verifier closes its stdin WITHOUT reading the request, then writes a schema-valid `deny code=malformed_input` at exit 0 — the shape §6 prescribes for a verifier that hits its request bound and stops reading. §2 obligates the host to write the entire request and then EOF stdin, so the read end can close under the host's write and surface as EPIPE/SIGPIPE — a request-delivery failure §7.2 does not enumerate among its fail-closed conditions. The host MUST reach a deny: either relay the verifier's deny or fail closed under its own classification of the write failure. Both are accepted (no verifier_code / failure_class pinned); what is caught is the host that crashes on the unhandled stdin write error, hangs waiting for a drain that never comes, or emits no decision at all. The assertion holds on both branches of the write/close race, so the vector is deterministic in verdict regardless of request size.
